Minors (N.H. RSA 276-A:4): the 16-17 35 h cap applies to weeks with 5 school days; 16-17 need a signed parental permission document on file. Under-16 limits are looser than federal 3 h/18 h/7 p.m. (federal.json still applies).

rules.summary: New Hampshire requires a 30-minute meal period for work over 5 hours.

citation.title: US DOL WHD — State meal-period requirements (rev. Jan. 1, 2023)
citation.excerpt: ½ hour, after 5 consecutive hours, unless feasible for employee to eat while working and is permitted to do so by employer

rules.summary: Youth under 16 may work at most 3 hours on school days (8 on non-school days) and 23 hours in a school week, 7 a.m.-9 p.m.

citation.title: N.H. RSA 276-A:4 — Youth Employment Law, prohibitions
citation.excerpt: No youth under 16 years of age shall be employed ... earlier than 7 o'clock a.m. or later than 9 o'clock p.m., more than 3 hours per day on school days and 23 hours per week during school weeks

rules.summary: During vacations, youth under 16 may work at most 8 hours a day and 48 hours a week, 7 a.m.-9 p.m.

citation.title: N.H. RSA 276-A:4 — Youth Employment Law, prohibitions
citation.excerpt: except that on nonschool days he may be employed 8 hours per day and, during vacations, 48 hours per week

rules.summary: Enrolled 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 35 hours in a work week when school is in session for 5 days.

citation.title: N.H. RSA 276-A:4 — Youth Employment Law, prohibitions
citation.excerpt: during which school is in session for 5 days, no youth 16 or 17 years of age who is duly enrolled in school shall work more than 35 hours during that work week

rules.summary: During school vacations, enrolled 16- and 17-year-olds may work at most 48 hours and 6 consecutive days a week.

citation.title: N.H. RSA 276-A:4 — Youth Employment Law, prohibitions
citation.excerpt: No youth 16 or 17 years of age who is duly enrolled in school shall work for more than 6 consecutive days or 48 hours in any one week during school vacations
